sentences.english: The farmer has a good dog.
That dog guards the large field.
But the dog sees a long shadow.
And so the small dog is frightened by the shadow.
But the farmer protects his own dog.

sentences.latin: Poeta clarus regi librum novum dat.
sentences.english: The famous poet gives the king a new book.

sentences.latin: Rex hoc donum laudat et poetam vocat.
sentences.english: The king praises this gift and calls the poet.

sentences.latin: Poeta felix ad solium regium vocatur.
sentences.english: The fortunate poet is called to the royal throne.

sentences.latin: Rex poetam fidelem amicum suum facit.
sentences.english: The king makes the loyal poet his own friend.

sentences.latin: Itaque poeta per omnem terram laudatur.
sentences.english: And so the poet is praised throughout the whole land.

sentences.latin: Iudex sapiens et fidelis leges veteres civitatis nostrae custodit.
sentences.english: The wise and loyal judge guards the old laws of our state.

sentences.latin: Sed tyrannus ferox edictum novum et grave populo dat.
sentences.english: But the fierce tyrant gives the people a new and harsh edict.

sentences.latin: Multi homines urbis magnae et pulchrae illo edicto terrentur.
sentences.english: Many men of the great and beautiful city are frightened by that edict.

sentences.latin: Sed veritas et libertas a iudice iusto et forti servantur.
sentences.english: But truth and freedom are protected by the just and brave judge.

sentences.latin: Itaque populus fortis iudicem bonum contra eum tyrannum servat.
sentences.english: And so the brave people protect the good judge against that tyrant.
